overview: The City Council approved key regulatory and redevelopment measures for Medford Square, authorized emergency capital funding for recreation facilities, and debated board appointment procedures under the city charter.

items.title: Approval of Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: Approved meeting records from February 24 and March 3, 2026, and a March 4 Committee of the Whole report on litigation strategy.

items.title: Grant of Location: 57 Swan Street
items.summary: Received and placed on file a petition from National Grid that was subsequently withdrawn by the petitioner.

items.title: Winthrop Street Snow Clearance Resolution
items.summary: Referred a resolution regarding snow clearance and legal reclassification of shared driveways at 553-569 Winthrop Street to the Committee on Public Works and Facilities. Residents and city officials discussed the safety risks of unplowed steep inclines and the legal barriers to using city resources on private land.

items.title: Resolution to Fund Medford Tree Canopy
items.summary: Approved a resolution urging the administration to fund the Urban Tree Management Plan and support volunteer planting initiatives to reach a 35% canopy cover goal. The measure addresses data showing a significant decline in the city's tree population and rising heat island effects in environmental justice communities.

items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
items.summary: Approved the appointments of John Dubuque and William Williams and the reappointments of Jennifer Keenan and John Lopes while rejecting the appointment of Sarah Berndt. The Council debated the administration's refusal to provide resumes or documentation for appointees, citing procedural requirements in the city charter.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund Appropriations
items.summary: Approved $160,000 for a moisture-resistant synthetic gym floor at the Chevalier Recreation Center and $9,995 for a used Zamboni. Recreation officials explained the emergency need for the floor following recurrent flooding that damaged the existing wood surface.

items.title: Medford Square Redevelopment Regulatory Vote
items.summary: Approved as amended the declaration of city-owned parcels in Medford Square as surplus and authorized a 99-year ground lease to Transom Real Estate. The order includes eminent domain authority strictly for the purpose of clearing complex title defects for the redevelopment project.

items.title: Medford Square City Hall Overlay District Referral
items.summary: Referred a proposed zoning amendment creating an overlay district for the Medford Square redevelopment parcels to the Community Development Board. The overlay is intended to facilitate specific project elements like a grocery store and housing by providing tailored dimensional and use regulations.
